> **Superseded in full by [REQ-020](REQ-020.md) (2026-06-02).** A legal review found that
> this REQ's entire purpose — the `lektion` field and the per-Lektion drag reorder view —
> *is* the prohibited pattern: it re-embodies a source compilation's selection/arrangement.

## Context

This REQ added a per-Lektion drag-reorder view to the console and a book-order new-card
consumer. It was superseded before it shipped to production (see REQ-020).

## Requirement

A scoped reorder view plus a book-order consumer for new-card introduction.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `VocabAdmin` exposes a **"Reihenfolge bearbeiten"** action that errors unless the
      changelist is filtered to exactly one Lektion. *Admin test
      (`test_reorder_requires_single_lektion_filter`, `test_reorder_renders_draggable_list`).*
- [x] Saving the reorder page rewrites `sequence` = 1..N over the reordered rows in one
      transaction. *Test `test_reorder_apply_rewrites_dense_sequence`.*
- [x] `learning/session.py` introduces new cards in `(lektion, sequence, id)` order, nulls
      last. *Session test (`test_new_cards_introduced_in_book_order`).*

## Notes

- The whole feature was reversed by REQ-020; this record is kept for the audit trail.
